svg.text: Low-side switch: the MOSFET connects the coil's return wire to ground. The coil is ALWAYS tied to +6 V.
GND ( MT3608 OUT− AND Nano GND — same rail )
legs, printed face toward you, left → right: G D S
2 · WHERE EACH LEAD GOES ON THE BREADBOARD
A “row” = one group of 5 holes on one side of the centre channel. These four rows must be four DIFFERENT rows.
Nothing else belongs in those rows. A stray lead sharing the GATE or DRAIN row is the usual reason it will not fire.
Black probe on the GND rail the whole time.
The drain falling 6.2 V → 0 V IS the switch closing.
If it never moves, the gate never got there.
Work down the list. Stop at the first failure.
· D5 wire in the wrong row
· 100 Ω not bridging D5 row → gate row
2. Gate is 3.3 V but drain stays 6.2 V
· legs misread — G D S left→right only with
· MOSFET straddling one row (all 3 legs shorted)
· source not reaching the GND rail
3. Drain drops but coil does not move
· one coil wire not in the +6 V row
· add the 1000 µF across +6 V / GND
· MT3608 OUT− and Nano GND not on the SAME rail
— this is the single most common miss
pull the D5 wire and touch the gate row
straight to +6 V. It must clunk.
